droptower.what_it_is: Lansmont Model 23 (M23) Shock Test System ('drop tower'): a programmable guided free-fall mechanical shock machine - an aluminium drop table (9.06 x 9.06 in top, 5x5 tapped-hole grid) with side bushing/brake housings rides on two chrome-plated steel guide rods, is lifted by an electric chain hoist via a solenoid latch head, and falls onto a pulse programmer / mat stack on a steel seismic base block; pneumatic brake pistons clamp the guide rods after rebound to prevent a second impact. Controlled by a Lansmont TouchTest Shock II table-top console with a Lansmont Test Partner 4 DAQ; fitted with the bungee acceleration kit. Belongs to Jeff Hill's SMASH Lab, BYU Clyde Building room CB 152A (not CB154); used by the tensegrity-optimization project for 60 in drops of ~0.1 m 3D-printed T3-prism tensegrity specimens.

overall_height.source: https://www.lansmont.com/sites/default/files/2025-10/M23%20Data%20Sheet.pdf ; vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization#27 (https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/issues/27#issuecomment-4408498939, attachment Lansmont_M23_Shock.pdf rev 4.6.20; copy in PR #28 branch copilot/add-drop-tower-picture: equipment/lansmont-m23/Lansmont_M23_Shock.pdf)
overall_height.quote_or_basis: "MACHINE ENVELOPE DIMENSIONS Height 96 – 120 in. (244 – 305 cm)" (96 in x 25.4 = 2438 mm; 120 in x 25.4 = 3048 mm). Height is a configurable range; the lab unit's configured height is not documented anywhere in the repos.

overall_height_lab_unit_estimate.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE. Hoist top nearly touches the room's drop ceiling in every full-tower view; Jeff says the tower can drop up to ~77 in without bungees, i.e. ~17 in more than the 60 in max of the 96-in-tall Lansmont Model 23 cushion tester, suggesting a ~110-115 in (2.8-2.9 m) build; pixel proportions (landed table block ~100 px = ~140 mm vs ~1780 px floor-to-top, with perspective compression at the top) give ~2.5-2.9 m. Best guess ~2.8 m.

overall_width_side_to_side.quote_or_basis: "Side to Side 21 in. (53 cm)" (21 x 25.4 = 533.4 mm). Envelope incl. protruding cylinders/pulleys.

overall_depth_front_to_back.quote_or_basis: "Front to Back 24 in. (61 cm)" (24 x 25.4 = 609.6 mm).

table_or_carriage_w.source: https://www.lansmont.com/sites/default/files/2025-10/M23%20Data%20Sheet.pdf ; vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization#27 (https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/issues/27#issuecomment-4408498939, attachment Lansmont_M23_Shock.pdf rev 4.6.20; copy in PR #28 branch copilot/add-drop-tower-picture: equipment/lansmont-m23/Lansmont_M23_Shock.pdf)
table_or_carriage_w.quote_or_basis: "TABLE DIMENSIONS Side to Side 9.06 in. (23 cm)" (9.06 x 25.4 = 230.1 mm). Top face of the aluminium drop table.

table_block_height.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE. Near-frontal 960-fps frame: table front face ~540 px tall vs ~905 px for the 230 mm table front edge -> ~137 mm; front-left view in lab_video_hook_carriage_latchhead_front.jpg corrected for ~45 deg foreshortening gives ~145 mm. Best ~140 mm; aluminium block with chamfered vertical corners.

table_top_hole_grid_pitch.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE. Top-down photo: 5 x 5 grid of tapped holes, centred, pitch = 150 of the 910 display px spanning the 230 mm table -> 37.9 mm, i.e. 1.5 in (38.1 mm); outer holes ~1.5 in from the table edges. Four corner holes carry socket-head anchor bolts with ~18-19 mm heads (consistent with 1/2 in SHCS - estimate).

table_tapped_hole_thread_nominal.quote_or_basis: LOW-CONFIDENCE ESTIMATE. Lab had to use rods '>10.5 mm' to cut threads matching 'the bolts we need for the drop tower', consistent with 1/2-13 UNC (12.7 mm) table holes; not confirmed.

carriage_overall_width_incl_side_housing.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE. Guide-rod bushing/brake housings are bolted to the left and right sides of the 230 mm table; rod axes ~140 mm either side of centre and housings extend ~40-60 mm beyond the rod axes.

carriage_side_housing_width.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE: each guide-rod bushing/brake housing bolted to a side of the table is ~60-80 mm wide (side to side).

carriage_side_housing_depth.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE: housing outer face spans most of the table depth (~190 mm) in the front-left view after ~45 deg foreshortening correction.

carriage_side_housing_height.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE: housing top stands ~30-50 mm above the table top; bottom roughly flush with the table underside.

brake_cover_disc_diameter.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE: round aluminium cover with 4 screws on each housing's outer face (brake piston), ~95 mm dia relative to the ~140 mm table block height.

guide_rod_count.quote_or_basis: COUNT, not mm. Two main chrome guide rods, one through each carriage side housing (left/right, at mid-depth). Photos also show one or two thinner auxiliary rods/bars at the right-rear (in Lansmont's design these carry the brake-trigger / instrument-trigger cams; HMI shows 'BRAKE TRIG' and 'INST TRIG') and one dark square-tube column at the right-rear. Lansmont: 'it travels on solid steel, chrome-plated Guide Rods ... also the surfaces that the shock table brake pistons act against'.

guide_rod_diameter.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE, best 25.4 mm (1 in). (a) Tape measure standing beside the rod (PR #67 IMG_6075): ~325 px/cm on the tape, rod ~790 px wide -> ~24 mm; (b) rod cross-hole for the 3/16 in (4.76 mm) locking pin is ~40-44 px vs rod ~190 px -> 22-27 mm; (c) frontal frame: spacing/diameter = 949/82 px = 11.6 -> ~24-26 mm for a ~280-300 mm spacing. No official figure found.

guide_rod_spacing_center_to_center.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE, best ~280 mm, side to side. Top-down photo scaled by the 230 mm table: rod axes appear ~31 mm outboard of each table edge (-> 292 mm), minus ~5-10 % perspective because the bushing tops sit above the table top; frontal 960-fps frame with perspective correction gives ~290 mm.

guide_rod_locking_pin_diameter.quote_or_basis: "I believe the diameter is 3/16 in, the same as the other one we used measured" (3/16 x 25.4 = 4.76 mm); pins are Klein 601-6 / 601-10 cabinet-screwdriver shanks with the tip cut off, inserted through a cross-hole in each guide rod below the carriage during mat changes and stowed in a white 2-hole interlock 'park station' box on the bench.

max_drop_height.quote_or_basis: "Jeff mentioned we could remove the bungees and let it freefall from a taller height. It could go up to about 77\" drop" (77 x 25.4 = 1956 mm). Lab statement, not a Lansmont spec; Lansmont gives no max drop height for the M23 (only max velocity change 24-32 ft/s = 7.3-9.7 m/s, which includes rebound).

max_equivalent_drop_height_Model23C_cush.quote_or_basis: "Max. Equivalent Drop Height 60 in. (152 cm)" / "Min. Equivalent Drop Height 1 in. (2.5 cm)" for the Model 23 CUSHION TESTER (platen machine, 96 in tall, 18 x 18 in envelope) - a different product; shown only for context, do not attribute to the lab's M23.

standard_drop_height_used.quote_or_basis: "The plate + specimen falls 60 in and arrives at dv ~ 5.47 m/s"; pu-configs README: "bungees removed ... 60 in drop height" (60 x 25.4 = 1524 mm). Standard for the July-Sept 2026 validation/BO campaigns (free fall).

other_drop_heights_used.quote_or_basis: Earlier campaigns used 5, 10, 13, 15, 20 and 30 in (127-762 mm); 13 in was the June/early-July default (HMI shows 'DH: 13.00'); at 5 in the 1000 G trigger did not fire.

min_drop_height.quote_or_basis: No M23 figure published. Only the Model 23 cushion tester lists 'Min. Equivalent Drop Height 1 in. (2.5 cm)'. Lab has run 5 in (127 mm) drops.

brake_catch_height_above_stack.quote_or_basis: "the carriage rebounds at ~0.4x impact speed and is braked at ~2.1-2.4 g to a dead stop 130-150 mm above the felt" (+86 to +89 ms after impact). Derived from 960-fps video scaled on free-fall speed, so approximate.

seismic_base_w.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE, best ~280 mm. Dark grey steel/cast-iron block (Auburn: 'cast iron seismic base with dampers'); ~1.3-1.45x the 230 mm table width in the Lansmont M23 photo and ~1.2x the table block in the landed-carriage frame; the guide rods run down beside/in front of it to the base slab, so it is probably no wider than the rod spacing.

seismic_base_d.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE, best ~320 mm; roughly as deep as wide (cube-like in every view).

seismic_base_h.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE, best ~340 mm. ~250 px tall vs ~100 px for the ~140 mm table block in the landed frame; ~0.12 of the tower height in two independent full-tower views; Lansmont M23 photo (96 in machine) scales to ~400 mm.

base_plate_w.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE: dark steel base slab under the seismic block, extending ~80-100 mm beyond it on each side; must fit the 533 mm envelope with pulleys/cylinders.

base_plate_d.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE: must fit the 610 mm front-to-back envelope.

base_plate_thickness.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE: ~0.03-0.04 of tower height in the full-tower views. Base carries 2 white nylon bungee pulleys (~50-60 mm dia) at the front, silver pneumatic cylinders and dark grey hydraulic dampers beside the block, and a small white caster/roller at the front-left.

impact_surface_height_above_floor.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE: base plate + seismic block (~0.16-0.17 of tower height). A round black rubber pad (~100 mm dia, estimate) with a centre hole sits on the seismic-block top; the lab stacks 4 felt sheets + 1 cardboard (later 1/4 in and 1/2 in PU sheets, 6.35/12.7 mm) on it.

rear_column_square_tube.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE: one dark grey square steel tube (~65 mm) at the right-rear running floor-to-head, with a black slotted plastic strip (cable duct or height-encoder strip) on its front face; appears ~1.6-2.7x the guide-rod width. Not in Lansmont's stock M23 photo, so this may be a newer/older frame variant.

top_head_plate_height_above_floor.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE: dark top plate/head where the rods and rear column end, ~150-250 mm below the hoist top (~2.8 m est.).

hoist_body_length.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE: grey electric chain hoist lying horizontally across the top head (Lansmont: 'Lansmont Shock Test Systems utilize electric hoists for lifting and positioning the shock table'), ~1.6-2x the table width.

hoist_chain_container_diameter.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE: grey conical chain bucket ~150 mm dia x ~250 mm tall hanging below the front-left of the hoist; chain runs down to the latch head.

latch_head_width.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE: aluminium cross-bar riding on the guide rods, hung from the hoist chain; round solenoid (~100 mm dia) on the left end, MS circular connector on the right; pivoting hook engages an upstanding hook plate on the carriage; stays up when the carriage drops.

max_payload_kg.source: https://www.lansmont.com/sites/default/files/2025-10/M23%20Data%20Sheet.pdf ; vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization#27 (https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/issues/27#issuecomment-4408498939, attachment Lansmont_M23_Shock.pdf rev 4.6.20; copy in PR #28 branch copilot/add-drop-tower-picture: equipment/lansmont-m23/Lansmont_M23_Shock.pdf)
max_payload_kg.quote_or_basis: VALUE IN kg, not mm. "MAXIMUM PAYLOAD 80 lbs. (36 kg)" (80 x 0.4536 = 36.3 kg).

tp4_daq_8ch_box_w.quote_or_basis: "8-CH ... Dimensions (W x D x H) 9.2\" x 7.9\" x 3.7\"" (9.2 x 25.4 = 233.7 mm); 16/24/32-CH units are 13.9 x 10.6 x 6.3 in. Bench equipment next to the tower; lab unit's channel count not confirmed (sessions in PR #67 use CH1-CH8).

specimen_max_height_T3_prism.quote_or_basis: "Tensegrity T3 prism | <=81 x 79 x 104 mm, 18-23 g"; BO bounds R 25-40 mm, H 60-110 mm before print scaling. Specimens are ~0.1 m (not ~1 m) - useful scale reference in table-top photos.

carriage_underside_height_above_floor_at.quote_or_basis: ESTIMATE: 1524 mm drop + ~420-520 mm mat/seismic top height; use to pose the raised carriage.

lab_cage_threaded_rod_length.quote_or_basis: "cutting it to the right length (~18 in we are thinking), and then adding threads" (18 x 25.4 = 457 mm); lab-built fixture of two acrylic plates + 4 threaded rods screwed into the table (used May-July 2026).

calibration_grid_square.quote_or_basis: "The vertical measurement of each black and white segment is 20mm" - checkerboard placed behind the tower for 960-fps video; distance from the tower varies, so it is not a direct scale for the tower.

droptower.notes: MODEL: Lansmont Model 23 (M23) Shock Test System, confirmed by Jeff Hill's brochure in #27 and PR #28 (equipment/lansmont-m23/); lab photos show the TouchTest Shock II table-top console named in that brochure (Beijer X2 base HMI) and a Lansmont Test Partner 4 DAQ (brochure: 'communicate seamlessly with Test Partner Data Acquisition Systems'). It is a guided free-fall shock machine (table on 2 guide rods, electric chain hoist, solenoid latch, pneumatic rod brakes, seismic base), NOT a Lansmont PDT package drop tester, and not the 23C cushion tester, 23D (magnesium carriage) or HC23. The lab unit carries the bungee 'acceleration kit' (white elastic cords over pulleys on the base) - 'bungee assisted' per docs/drop-test-protocol.md - but bungees were removed for the 60-in free-fall campaigns. The frame differs from Lansmont's stock M23 photo (dark square column at right-rear with slotted strip; no large programmer cylinder - the lab drops onto felt/PU mat stacks on a rubber pad on the seismic block), so it may be a different vintage or configuration; the P23 web image looks similar but nothing in the repos says P23. LOCATION: Jeff Hill's SMASH Lab, BYU Clyde Building room CB 152A (#90 comment 5198260416: 'installed into the drop tower computer in CB 152A'; PC desktop shows 'SMASH Lab'/'SMASHGun'). It is NOT in the VCL's CB154; byu-vcl lab-models/README.md already notes it is modelled but not placed. In the room it stands against a wall right of a wooden workbench (PC, TP4, TouchTest console), with a blue Modal Shop shaker stand in front-left and a stainless/blue cabinet (the slug-gun impact enclosure) to the right; hoist top is just under the drop ceiling. USE: tensegrity-optimization drop tests of 3D-printed T3-prism specimens (<=81 x 79 x 104 mm, 18-23 g) bolted/tied onto the table (lab acrylic plate/cage, key-seat accelerometer mounts); standard 60 in (1524 mm) free-fall onto 4 felt + 1 cardboard, later 1/4 or 1/2 in PU sheets; ~3,660 physical drops through 2026-08-19 per #101. Impact speed ~5.47 m/s at 60 in. Falling (carriage) mass has never been weighed (#88/#94). OFFICIAL SPECS (M23 data sheet / brochure 4.6.20): table 9.06 x 9.06 in (23 x 23 cm); envelope H 96-120 in (244-305 cm) x 21 in (53 cm) side-to-side x 24 in (61 cm) front-to-back; max acceleration 5000 g; min pulse 0.25 ms half-sine; max velocity change 24-32 ft/s (7.3-9.7 m/s); max payload 80 lb (36 kg); half-sine standard, trapezoidal and terminal-peak sawtooth with optional programmers; machine power 200-240 VAC 3-phase >=4 A or 380-480 VAC 3-phase >=2 A; controller 100-120 or 200-240 VAC 1-phase >=1 A; plant air 90 psi (6.2 bar); nitrogen 1000-2000 psi only for the optional DB programmer.
